I am 62 years old. I finished middle school and came back to the village to farm. I have 16.1 mu of flat good land in Quzhou, and I have done wheat-maize rotation on this same land for 40 years. I know every corner of these fields.

For winter wheat, I will plant the same improved variety I bought last year from the seed dealer in town — it is the one my neighbors are all using. Before sowing in October, I will spread one full bag of compound fertilizer on each mu, that is 50 kg per mu of the 15-15-15 kind. Then I will run the rotary tiller to mix it in. I sow about 15 jin of wheat seed per mu. In the spring, when the wheat turns green and starts to joint, I will topdress with half a bag of urea per mu — 25 kg. Some people put less to save money, but I would rather put a bit too much than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings, once at jointing in March, and once at grain filling in May. I have a well, so I pump the water myself. For pesticides, I spray herbicide once in early spring, and I spray insecticide twice — once when the aphids come and once later when the weather warms up. I expect 520 kg per mu this year if the frost does not hurt us.

For summer maize, right after I cut wheat in early June, I hire a machine to rotary till the stubble and sow hybrid maize seed. I put 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer — one bag per mu, same as wheat. At the big trumpet stage, when the plants are knee-high and hungry, I topdress with 30 kg of urea per mu. Last year I only put 20 kg and the leaf tips turned yellow by August, so this year I am putting 30 kg to be safe. I irrigate twice: once right after sowing if the soil is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage when the heat hits. Maize cannot wait for water in July. I spray herbicide once after sowing, and I spray insecticide twice for corn borer. I expect 560 kg per mu.

My wife and I do most of the work, but for harvest and sowing I hire machines. The whole 16.1 mu goes to wheat first, then maize on the same land. Diesel for the pump and machine hire are my main costs. I watch what my neighbors do. If everyone on this side of the village puts more urea this year, I will do the same — they are not fools.
